title: Make Command Center Lab startup minimal and orchestrator-driven
description: Implement the operator-directed lifecycle correction revealed during the roles-roadmap run. Default CCL startup must open only the operator surfaces and one core Codex orchestrator; Claude, scout/helper, Pi, and Librarian lanes remain available on demand but do not auto-start. The orchestrator prompt must route from SQLite/runner, start only bounded visible workers when work requires them, mark finished identities standby or terminal, avoid replacement rotation when no live claim remains, and preserve all no-headless, approval, privacy, review-separation, and continuity safeguards. Do not bind permanent providers to organizational roles.
acceptance_criteria: Default CCL topology starts Shell, Monitor, and one Codex orchestrator only; Claude, Pi, Librarian, and scout/helper launchers remain available but are not automatically opened.

The Codex orchestrator startup contract routes from canonical SQLite and runner state, uses visible wezterm-tab workers only when needed, and records durable progress without treating open terminals as availability truth.
Completed or review-waiting workers are durably placed in standby or terminal state and no replacement rotation is launched when an identity has no live claim or continuation obligation.
Focused tests prove default topology, preserved on-demand launchers, no fixed provider-to-role binding, no headless launch path, and no regression to Monitor/Shell availability.
Delivery evidence documents migration, rollback, residual privacy/approval boundaries, and the distinction between orchestrator routing and autonomous authority.
